description: Divination reflects the important role that religion played in the military and political life of many ancient civilizations. Greeks consulted oracles and seers and examined sacrificial omens, Romans relied on augurs and haruspices, Persians and other Iranian peoples looked to priestly interpretation of ritual and celestial signs, while Carthaginians, Egyptians, Indians, and other cultures maintained their own traditions of prophecy, omen-reading, and sacred consultation. Before battles, journeys, treaties, and major public decisions, rulers and commanders often sought signs of divine approval, making divination a practical part of leadership as well as an expression of religious belief.
